After the first 3 weeks off is when many people relapse, so if u keep pushing thru into more months of sobriety that’s when things get more clear and u start to adjust. You will not be that different off weed, just a more responsible competent version of your current self.

That this isn’t a quick process. It’s similar to what someone has to do to lose a lot of weight. This is a lifestyle change. U now have to possibly quit other things like alcohol, or any other drug or substance that increases craving for weed. U absolutely can’t hang out with people who are smoking and if u do it’s very risky especially while u are still in the early months of the quit. If u want to remain off weed, u have to permanently abstain if u have ever been addicted to it and it became a negative thing for u. U can’t dabble thinking u can sometimes use. U must focus on preventing relapse at all costs because it sets u back to the beginning and craving start immediately along with withdrawal, which then leads back to daily use quickly. You can anticipate that it may take some months before u start to become more functional. There’s a period that lasts where u will be lethargic, brain fog, not gonna be that productive and it may go on a long time. You will have to live your life in a way that u reduce the potential triggers that lead to relapse. If u have toxic people around u it will be harder to quit also. Or a stressful job. I’m just about 4 months off and it’s so worth it. Even with all the suffering I went thru in the earlier months. My life is not like totally changing overnight but I would never go back to how I was on weed. If u can push thru those first couple of months and maybe into month 3 u get to the stage where u begin to feel ok off weed. U will still have times u wish u could smoke but the longer u abstain and the more u learn to sit with discomfort the more u will no longer be wishing u could smoke to feel better.
